items.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about 'The King' hearing about Miller Rapper, and later mentions 'This king, Janaka' in a separate anecdote. The interviewee (Charles Lloyd) is recounting historical/legendary figures and does not express a personal relationship with any specific 'King'.

ctx.x: Miller Rapper was 10th, 11th, 13th century Buddhist deity, who... His mother had... his father died and the family took everything away from his mother and the brothers did, and she was left homeless and stuff like that. So Miller Rapper got upset, he went away and learned black magic, came back, wreaked havoc on the area, blew the whole thing up. And then he realized that after awhile that black magic wasn't a way for him to go, and he wanted to clean up so he wanted the way of the white cloud. He realized he…
